web_evidence.title: A FIRE & BLOOD Excerpt just for YOU!
web_evidence.note: Martin identifies Archmaester Gyldayn as the book's perspective, and the long authorized interior excerpt sustains external third-person historical narration. Its first-person material is explicitly contained in dialogue and Alysanne's quoted letter.

web_evidence.title: Fire & Blood (HBO Tie-in Edition)
web_evidence.note: The publisher describes the entire work as a Targaryen chronicle related by a learned maester and notes that Gyldayn writes centuries after the events, establishing an external, nonparticipating historical narrator.

web_evidence.title: Fire & Blood: 6 Game of Thrones Easter Eggs from George R.R. Martin’s New Book
web_evidence.note: This review explicitly reports that the book has one narrator, Archmaester Gyldayn, whose retrospective historical account is distinct from the participating POV-character structure of the main novels.

web_evidence.title: About Fire and Blood by George R. R. Martin
web_evidence.note: The literary overview names Gyldayn as narrator and explicitly classifies the book's point of view as third person.

search_log: Searched site:georgerrmartin.com for "Fire and Blood" excerpt and Gyldayn; opened Martin's authorized 2018 excerpt and verified sustained interior third-person chronicle prose.
Searched Penguin Random House for the title and opened the publisher page; it describes the whole work as a chronicle related by a maester writing centuries after the events.

Searched "Fire and Blood narrator Archmaester Gyldayn point of view" and "Fire & Blood first person third person narration Gyldayn"; opened Vanity Fair, The Guardian, and Book Analysis descriptions, which consistently identify Gyldayn's retrospective historical narration, with Book Analysis explicitly saying third person.

Ran exact-quotation searches for "Then the storm broke, and the dragons danced," "Let no man think that the fire of the Targaryens," and "The next morning the sea was calm again" to test whether apparent first person was base narration; results corroborated the first two as chronicler narration, while the last appeared only in quote reposts and was reconciled structurally as embedded eyewitness speech.
Search results from fan wikis, Reddit, quote-image sites, Goodreads, and inaccessible or unauthorized previews were treated as discovery or dead ends and not used as controlling evidence.
person_note: Fire & Blood is framed as Archmaester Gyldayn's retrospective history. He narrates Targaryen figures and events externally and did not participate in the centuries-earlier action, so the controlling person is THIRD under the participation-based definition. The sampled event passages agree with that chronicler position. Numerous I, we, and you forms occur in dialogue, reported testimony, sayings, and source documents; q02437's my brother recollection is necessarily an embedded eyewitness voice, not Gyldayn, and does not create a sustained first-person base section. The authorized excerpt likewise embeds a first-person letter inside continuous third-person history. No credible source indicates alternating base-person sections; the remaining uncertainty is limited to missing quotation boundaries in isolated popular quotes, not the whole-book structure.
